name: Nicias
bio: Nicias is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors dates the poet to 3rd century BC. Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of Meleager's Wreath, the Garland compiled about 100 BC.
This archive carries the 3 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the first volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Books I–VI) (Book VI: 122, 127, 270).

poems.title: Book VI, 122
poems.author: Nicias
poems.text: Maenap of Ares, sustainer of war, impetuous spear, who now hath set thee here, a gift to the goddess who awakes the battle? “Menius ; for springing lightly from his hand in the forefront of the fight I wrought havoc among the Odrysae on the plain.”

poems.title: Book VI, 127: A Shield speaks
poems.author: Nicias
poems.text: So one day I was fated to leave the hideous field of battle and listen to the song and dance of girls round the temple of Artemis, where Epixenus set me, when white old age began to wear out his limbs.

poems.title: Book VI, 270
poems.author: Nicias
poems.text: The head-kerchief and water-blue veil of Amphareta rest on thy head, Ilithyia ; for them she vowed to thee when she prayed thee to keep dreadful death far away from her in her labour.

poems.title: Book VII, 200
poems.author: Nicias
poems.text: No longer curled under the leafy branch shall I delight in sending forth a voice from my tender wings. For I fell into the . . . hand of a boy, who caught me stealthily as I was seated on the green leaves.

poems.title: Book IX, 315
poems.author: Nicias
poems.text: Sit here under the poplar trees, traveller, for thou art weary, and come near and drink from my fountain. When thou art far away bethink thee of the spring near which stands Simus’ statue beside his dead son Gillus.

poems.title: Book IX, 564
poems.author: Nicias
poems.text: Bee, that revealest the presence of many-coloured spring in her delightful bloom ; yellow bee, revelling in the prime of the flowers; fly to the sweetly-scented field and busy thyself with thy work, that thy waxen chambers may be filled.

poems.title: Book XVI, 188: On Another
poems.author: Nicias
poems.text: I, Hermus, whose domain is Cyllene’s steep, forest-clad hill, stand here guarding the pleasant playground; and on me the boys often set marjoram and hyacinths and fresh wreaths of violets.

poems.title: Book XVI, 189: On a Statue of Pan
poems.author: Nicias
poems.text: Having left the slopes of Maenalus I abide here, for Peristratus’ sake, to guard the hives, on the watch for him who would rob the bees. But keep clear of my hand and the nimble stride of my country-bred shanks.

poems.title: To the Milesian Artemis (Mackail)
poems.author: Nicias
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: So I was destined, I also, once to abandon the hateful strife of Ares and hear the maiden choirs around Artemis' temple, where Epixenus placed me when white old age began to waste his limbs.

poems.title: On a Wayside Tomb (Mackail)
poems.author: Nicias
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Sit beneath the poplars here, traveller, when thou art weary, and drawing nigh drink of our spring; and even far away remember the fountain that Simus sets by the side of Gillus his dead child.

poems.title: Below Cyllene (Mackail)
poems.author: Nicias
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: I who inherit the tossing mountain-forests of steep Cyllene, stand here guarding the pleasant playing fields, Hermes, to whom boys often offer marjoram and hyacinth and fresh garlands of violets.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.122: μαινὰς Ἐνυαλίου, πολεμαδόκε, θοῦρι
poems.author: Nicias
poems.text:
μαινὰς Ἐνυαλίου, πολεμαδόκε, θοῦρι κράνεια,
τίς νύ σε θῆκε θεᾷ δῶρον ἐγερσιμάχᾳ;
“μήνιος· ἦ γὰρ τοῦ παλάμας ἄπο ῥίμφα θοροῦσα
ἐν προμάχοις Ὀδρύσας δήιον ἀμπεδίον.”

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.127: μέλλον ἄρα στυγερὰν κἀγώ
poems.author: Nicias
poems.text:
μέλλον ἄρα στυγερὰν κἀγώ ποτε δῆριν Ἄρηος
ἐκπρολιπγοῦσα χορῶν παρθενίων ἀΐειν
Ἀρτέμιδος περὶ ναόν, Ἐπίξενος ἔνθα μʼ ἔθηκεν,
λευκὸν ἐπεὶ κείνου γῆρας ἔτειρε μέλη.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.270: Ἀμφαρέτας κρήδεμνα καὶ ὑδατόεσσα
poems.author: Nicias
poems.text:
Ἀμφαρέτας κρήδεμνα καὶ ὑδατόεσσα καλύπτρα,
Εἰλείθυια, τεᾶς κεῖται ὑπὲρ κεφαλᾶς,
ἇς σε μετʼ ἐκαλέσσατο λευγαλέας οἱ
κῆρας ἀπʼ ὠδίνων τῆλε βαλεῖν λοχίων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.200: οὐκέτι δὴ τανύφυλλον ὑπὸ
poems.author: Nicias
poems.text:
οὐκέτι δὴ τανύφυλλον ὑπὸ κλάκα κλωνὸς ἑλιχθεὶς
τέρψομʼ ἀπὸ ῥαδινῶν φθόγγον ἱεὶς πτερύγων·
χεῖρα γὰρ εἰς † ἀρετὰν παιδὸς πέσον, ὅς με λαθραίως
μάρψεν, ἐπὶ χλωρῶν ἑζόμενον πετάλων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.315: ἵζευ ὑπʼ αἰγείροισιν, ἐπεὶ
poems.author: Nicias
poems.text:
ἵζευ ὑπʼ αἰγείροισιν, ἐπεὶ κάμες, ἐνθάδʼ, ὁδῖτα,
καὶ πῖθʼ ἆσσον ἰὼν πίδακος ἁμετέρας·
μνᾶσαι δὲ κράναν καὶ ἀπόπροθι, ᾇ ˘ ἔπι Γίλλῳ
Σῖμος ἀποφθιμένῳ παιδὶ παριδρύεται.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.564: Αἰόλον ἱμεροθαλὲς ἔαρ φαίνουσα
poems.author: Nicias
poems.text:
Αἰόλον ἱμεροθαλὲς ἔαρ φαίνουσα, μέλισσα
ξουθά, ἐφʼ ὡραίοις ἄνθεσι μαινομένα,
χῶρον ἐφʼ ἡδύπνοον πωτωμένα, ἔργα τίθευ σύ,
ὄφρα τεὸς πλήθῃ κηροπαγὴς θάλαμος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.188: εἰνοσίφυλλον ὄρος Κυλλήνιον αἰπὺ
poems.author: Nicias
poems.text:
εἰνοσίφυλλον ὄρος Κυλλήνιον αἰπὺ λελογχώς,
τῇδʼ ἕστηκʼ ἐρατοῦ γυμνασίου μεδέων,
Ἑρμῆς· ᾧ ἔπι παῖδες ἀμάρακον ἠδʼ ὑάκινθον
πολλάκι, καὶ θαλεροὺς θῆκαν ἴων στεφάνους.
